summary: Updates RFC 2026 to stop using STD 1 as a summary of Internet Official Protocol Standards. It obsoletes RFC 5000 and asks the IESG to move RFC 5000 and STD 1 to Historic status.

plainLanguage.summary: This Best Current Practice retires the requirement to publish a separate summary of Internet standards. The RFC Editor's online list and the IESG's minutes already provide the information the old documents were meant to supply.

subtitle: The IETF retires STD 1, the periodically published summary of Internet standards.

tldr.problem: RFC 2026 called for a periodic standards summary, but the document had not been kept current and readers used the RFC Editor's online list.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7100 removes the relevant summary requirements from RFC 2026, obsoletes RFC 5000 and asks the IESG to move it and STD 1 to Historic status.
tldr.outcome: The online list replaces the summary, and IESG minutes serve as the record of standards actions. RFC 7100 updates RFC 2026.

today: RFC 7100 is a Best Current Practice. It obsoletes RFC 5000 and updates RFC 2026; the unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why STD 1 Is Retired
sections.content:
RFC 2026 and its predecessors called for periodic publication of an RFC summarizing the status of Internet protocol and service specifications. The summary was known as STD 1; its latest version at the time was RFC 5000.

RFC 7100 says the summary had not been kept up to date and had fallen out of use in favor of the RFC Editor's online list. The IETF no longer saw a need to maintain the separate document.
sections.plainLanguage: The separate standards summary was out of date, while the RFC Editor's online list was being used instead. The IETF decided that it no longer needed to maintain the summary.

sections.title: Changes to the Standards Process
sections.content:
RFC 7100 updates RFC 2026 by removing the paragraphs that call for the standards summary in Sections 2.1, 3.3 and 6.1.3. It also obsoletes RFC 5000 and asks the Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG) to move RFC 5000 and STD 1 to Historic status.

RFC 2026 also called for a newsletter summary of completed and pending standards actions. RFC 7100 says the IESG minutes had become the publication of record, so it removes that requirement too.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo removes the old instructions to publish the standards summary and a newsletter report. It names the online list and IESG minutes as the sources already serving those purposes.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that this process change does not impact the security of the Internet. It changes publication requirements rather than protocol behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: This change is about publishing standards information. The RFC says it does not affect Internet security.

references.text: Bradner, S., "The Internet Standards Process -- Revision 3", BCP 9, RFC 2026, October 1996.
RFC Editor, "Internet Official Protocol Standards", RFC 5000, May 2008.
